subject: Cutover and Split-Site Addendum — renewal sequencing & approval
messages:
From: Liam Carter <liam.carter@medsync.io>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: sre@medsync.io, procurement@medsync.io
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Add isolated on-prem pod + region at renewal (May)

Hi Jasmine —

As we approach our May renewal, the architecture team has signed off on carving out a physically isolated pod for our analytics workloads. We need two things included in the renewal: (1) a new on-prem cluster (3x A100 equiv nodes) deployed in our Salt Lake City colo, and (2) an additional VPC-isolated region in us-west-2 for disaster recovery and regulatory separation.

Key asks:
- Target cutover during the renewal window (May 12–20).
- Separate tenancy (no shared KV prefixes) for analytics cluster.
- SLA uplift for the analytics cluster during business hours (SLA language will be part of the addendum).

I've attached the network diagram and a brief runbook we put together. Can you share a rough delta on pricing and a proposed sequencing plan (canary -> stage -> full)? Procurement is copied for commercial and PO timing.

Thanks —
Liam
Liam Carter
Head of Platform Engineering, Medsync Health

Folks —

I pulled a short technical sketch for the canary and cutover. High-level plan:

1) Canary (2 weeks): deploy 1 node of the analytics cluster in SLC, enable KV namespace isolation, route 5% of analytics jobs (non-PII) to canary. Smoke tests + perf baseline.
2) Stage (4 days): expand to 2 nodes, increase job routing to 25%, run full E2E ETL window.
3) Full cutover: expand to 3-node cluster, switch production routing, decommission temporary peering for the legacy analytics pool.

Requirements / blockers:
- Colocation VLAN must support jumbo MTU (confirmed with SLC colo?)
- We’ll need a one-hour maintenance window for final switch (overnight preferred).
- Backup/export snapshot plan for KV namespaces to be executed pre-cutover.

I also drafted a minimal canary runbook. Attaching stub. Connor

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
